messages:
josh: :rotating_light: incident-bot alerted - p99 serving latency spike on dedicated-usw2 pools, queue depth rising. Paging oncall.
incident-bot: Alert ID: INC-2067. Detected p99_stream_latency > 1200ms for 3m. Affected route: /v1/generate (streaming). Pools: dedicated-usw2-3, dedicated-usw2-4.
josh: I'm paged. digging. initial look: autoscaler didn't spin up warmup nodes quickly. queue depth ~ 4k across region. customers reporting streaming stalls.
maria: I see increased warmup_timeouts in autoscale logs: warmup_handshake_timeout_ms=120000 and several TLS handshake retries.
ravi: oncall takeover in 10m? I'm available. josh - handoff details?
josh: handing off to ravi. summary: p99 ~2.8s, streaming stalls reported by customers, fallback to non-streaming path increases token latency and changes semantics. Manual mitigations to consider: manual scale, divert to hosted region, enable quantized fallback model, temporary rate-limits.
samira: adding context: traffic burst from tenant AcmeCorp prod at ~17:02 UTC, sustained 55-70 req/s for ~4m. likely amplification from client SDK retries.
lee: grabbing metrics - queue_depth by pool:
```
pool dedicated-usw2-3: depth=1200, warmup_in_progress=1
pool dedicated-usw2-4: depth=900, warmup_in_progress=1
scaling_events: autoscaler requested +4 nodes at 17:03, provisioning started 17:03:30, handshake failed at 17:05:30
```
ops-bot: Autoscaler log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-14T17:05:30Z] warn autoscaler: warmup handshake timeout (id=wk-394, timeout_ms=120000)
[2026-03-14T17:05:31Z] info autoscaler: retrying launch, backoff=15s
```
ravi: immediate actions I'm going to run: 1) manual scale pool +3 nodes to reduce queue; 2) enable model-quantized fallback for streaming endpoints to speed warmup; 3) apply temp rate-limit for AcmeCorp to moderate burst. I'll execute now and report.
josh: drop PD link and brief customer-facing note, will loop in success.
ravi: executing manual scale now:
```
rbctl pool scale --pool-id dedicated-usw2-3 --delta 3 --reason "incident manual scale"
```
maria: while nodes come up, recommend disabling streaming for /v1/generate on those pools to avoid stalls (streaming path seems more sensitive to warmup stalls). quick config:
```
route /v1/generate {
  streaming: false
}
```
samira: notifying Customer Success and flagging AcmeCorp. sending: "We're investigating increased latency and streaming stalls; temporary mitigations are in progress." :phone:
ops-bot: manual scale accepted, new instances enrolling. warmup_progress: 40%
lee: after enabling non-streaming path p95 improved to ~450ms at 17:09, p99 still ~1.1s. queue_depth trending down.
ravi: warmup finished for manual nodes at 17:12, handshake errors dropped.
```
[2026-03-14T17:12:10Z] info node wk-397: ready
```
josh: rerouting traffic off the impacted pools to reduce tail pressure.
maria: post-mitigations snapshot: p95 320ms, p99 520ms. queue_depth <200 across pools. streaming disabled for affected route.
ravi: proposed follow-ups: 1) infra to root-cause autoscale handshake timeouts (possible host kernel/TLS config or AMI issue); 2) add warmup fallback to a smaller quantized model when handshake fails; 3) introduce a faster-provision policy for sudden bursts (pre-warm smaller instances); 4) add automated temporary throttle for tenants generating bursts. Owner: ravi. ETA: 72h for RCA and action plan.
samira: I'll own the customer comms for AcmeCorp and prepare a status update template.
josh: thanks team. leaving notes on PD: https://pagerduty/INC-2067
incident-bot: Incident INC-2067 -> status: mitigated (partial). Recommended next step: oncall to run RCA and schedule postmortem.
ravi: taking incident to postmortem. handing oncall to lee for monitoring for 1h. passing handoff.
lee: ack — monitoring dashboards and will escalate if regressions happen.
